items.content_excerpt: $NVDA “If I had invested $10,000 in NVIDIA in 2015, I would have $2.97 million today.” It’s not that simple. To get there, you would have had to invest $10,000 and watch it turn into $16,000 and do nothing. Then $53,000, then $140,000. Then it fell over 60% to $66,300. Would you have held? If so, you would then watch that $66,300 turn into $649,000. Would you have sold then? Turning 10K in to 650k? If not, you'd see that $649,000 drop to a heartbreaking $241,000. Over 400K lost. What would you have done? Posted on Stocktwits shorting and finding gossip to make yourself feel better? If you held, you would then watch that $241,000 turn into $4.54 million. That's the top. Would you have sold? If not, you just saw it drop back down to $2.97 million. So will you sell now? Risk going all the way back to 10k? Earning in this market takes patience, a will of steal, and brains. Volatility is the price the market demands for access to long-term returns. $META $GOOG $AAPL

items.content_excerpt: Palo Alto Networks is facing a federal lawsuit accusing the cybersecurity company of accounting fraud, adding pressure to its shares amid concerns over a recently announced $4.5 billion acquisition. The complaint was filed by former regional vice president Dan McGill in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. He alleges that company executives encouraged resellers to submit purchase orders before receiving formal customer approval, allowing transactions to be recorded as completed sales and potentially inflating reported revenue. McGill also claims he was wrongfully dismissed after raising concerns internally. Palo Alto Networks has not publicly responded to the allegations. Investor concerns are also focused on the company's $4.5 billion all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute, announced days before the lawsuit emerged, with potential dilution and integration risks. $PANW
